examples.en: The hunter chased a deer in the forest.
The hunter climbed the mountain at dawn.
I read a story about a hunter and a tiger.
He is famous as an experienced hunter.
The rabbit chased by the hunter hid in a burrow.
The child who followed the hunter got lost.

explain: 동사는 '사냥하다'이고, 사냥하는 사람을 '사냥꾼'이라고 해요. 옛이야기에서는 '포수'라는 말도 나와요. '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 직업이나 습관처럼 하는 사람에게 붙는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 옛이야기에 포수가 호랑이를 만나는 이야기가 나와요.
phrases.en: There is an old tale where a hunter meets a tiger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛이야기에서 총으로 사냥하는 사람을 말하는 옛날식 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An old-fashioned word for a hunter with a gun, seen in old tales.

phrases.en: The hunter hunts wild boar in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사냥꾼이 하는 일을 나타내는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for what a hunter does.

phrases.en: The hunter went up the mountain with his hunting dog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사냥 이야기에서 함께 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair that often appears together in hunting stories.

explain_en: The verb is '사냥하다', and the person who hunts is a '사냥꾼'. In old tales you may also see the word '포수'. The suffix '-꾼' is added to a person who does something as a job or habit.

en: to be deleted; to be removed; to be eliminated

examples.en: The file got deleted because I pressed it by mistake.
Old messages are deleted automatically.
I hope my post isn't deleted.
Save the photos before they are deleted.

examples.ko: 삭제된 파일은 휴지통에서 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can find deleted files in the trash.
This comment will be deleted soon.

explain: 컴퓨터나 인터넷의 글, 파일이 지워질 때 써요. 지우는 사람이 주어이면 '삭제하다'예요. 연필로 쓴 글씨는 보통 '지우다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I delete photos I don't need.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지우는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person deleting is the subject.

phrases.en: The file won't be deleted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지워지지 않을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form for when something won't get removed.

phrases.en: If you press the delete button, the post is removed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터 화면에서 자주 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation often seen on computer screens.

explain_en: Use it when files or posts on a computer or the internet are removed. If a person is the subject, use '삭제하다'. For pencil writing, people usually say '지우다'.

examples.ko: 손님은 직원을 따라 창가 자리로 안내됐어요.
examples.en: The guest was shown to a seat by the window.
Details will be sent to you by text.

examples.ko: 안내된 장소로 가니 직원이 기다리고 있었어요.
examples.en: When I went to the place I was told, a staff member was waiting.

examples.ko: 화장실 위치가 안내되지 않아서 직원에게 물어봤어요.
examples.en: The restroom location wasn't indicated, so I asked a staff member.

examples.ko: 행사 시간이 안내돼 있으니 꼭 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: The event times are posted, so please be sure to check.
I'm waiting for the day the results are announced.

explain: 사람이 자리로 이끌려 가거나 정보를 전달받을 때 써요. 공지나 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '안내를 받다', '안내받다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Please go to the third floor as directed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알려 준 내용을 그대로 따르라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to follow the given instructions.

phrases.example: 사용 방법이 화면에 자세히 안내돼 있어요.
phrases.en: The instructions are explained in detail on the screen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명이 안내문에 잘 나와 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when information is clearly given in a notice.

phrases.en: The staff showed me to my seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '안내되다'보다 '안내받다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, 안내받다 sounds more natural than 안내되다.

explain_en: It is used when a person is led to a place or receives information, and you often see it in notices. In speech, 안내를 받다 or 안내받다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: I ran into an old love on the street.
When I hear this song, I think of an old love.
He still can't forget his old love.
I got a message from an old love after a long time.
I sorted out and threw away photos of my old love.
I ended up living in the same neighborhood as my old love.

explain: '첫사랑'은 처음 한 사랑이고, '옛사랑'은 지나간 사랑을 그리운 마음으로 부르는 말이에요. 일상에서 직접 '전 애인'이라고 하는 것보다 노래나 글에서 감성적으로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: On rainy days I miss my old love.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나간 사랑을 그리워하는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express longing for a past love.

phrases.en: I met my old love at a gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 사랑했던 사람과 다시 만날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when meeting someone you once loved.

phrases.en: I still haven't forgotten my old love.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나간 사랑을 마음에서 지운다는 뜻으로, 보통 '잊지 못하다'로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to put a past love out of your mind; often used as '잊지 못하다' (can't forget).

explain_en: '첫사랑' is your first love, while '옛사랑' is a past love remembered with some longing. It is more sentimental than the direct '전 애인' (ex-partner) and appears often in songs and writing.

en: to be accidental; to be casual; to be haphazard

examples.en: That chance meeting became a lasting bond.

examples.ko: 그 두 사건이 우연하지 않다는 얘기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: People said the two incidents were not a coincidence.
Something I started by chance became my job.
At first I thought it was all a coincidence.

examples.ko: 우연하게도 같은 날 같은 곳에 갔어요.
examples.en: By coincidence, we went to the same place on the same day.
It looks accidental, but it was actually planned.

explain: '우연히 만났어요'처럼 부사 '우연히'로 쓰거나 '우연이에요'로 말하기도 해요. '우연하다'는 '우연한 만남'처럼 명사를 꾸밀 때 자연스러워요. 반대는 '필연'이에요.

phrases.en: I ran into an old friend on the street by chance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 앞에서 '뜻하지 않게'라는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, placed before a verb to mean 'unexpectedly'.

phrases.example: 그 두 일이 한꺼번에 생긴 건 우연하지 않아요.
phrases.en: It is not accidental that those two things happened at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우연이 아니라 이유가 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is not chance but has a reason.

phrases.example: 우연한 기회에 그 책을 읽게 됐어요.
phrases.en: I came to read that book through a chance opportunity.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우연하다'가 명사를 꾸미는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural phrase where 우연하다 describes a noun.

explain_en: You can say '우연히 만났어요' with the adverb, or '우연이에요'. 'Uyeonhada' sounds natural when describing a noun, as in '우연한 만남'. The opposite idea is '필연' (inevitability).

examples.ko: 길을 아니까 오늘은 제가 운전석에 앉을게요.
examples.en: I know the way, so I will sit in the driver's seat today.

examples.ko: 차 운전석 문이 갑자기 안 열려요.
examples.en: The driver's door of the car suddenly will not open.

examples.ko: 키가 작아서 운전석 의자를 앞으로 당겼어요.
examples.en: I am short, so I moved the driver's seat forward.

examples.ko: 높은 차는 운전석에 앉으면 시야가 넓어요.
examples.en: In a tall car, you get a wide view when you sit in the driver's seat.
There is a map on the seat next to the driver.

examples.ko: 택시 기사님이 운전석에서 내려서 문을 열어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The taxi driver got out of the driver's seat and opened the door for me.

explain: 운전석 옆자리는 '조수석'이라고 해요. '조수'는 돕는 사람이라는 뜻인데, 지금은 운전을 돕지 않아도 그대로 써요. 한국은 차가 길 오른쪽으로 달려서 운전석이 왼쪽에 있어요.

phrases.en: I sat in the driver's seat and buckled up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전을 하려고 자리에 앉는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes sitting down to drive.

phrases.en: I'll sit in the passenger seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전석 옆자리를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The seat next to the driver's seat.

phrases.en: Please open the window on the driver's side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차의 운전하는 사람 쪽을 말할 때 '쪽'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 쪽 to mean the driver's side of the car.

explain_en: The seat next to the driver is called '조수석'. '조수' means 'assistant', but the word stays even when the person is not helping to drive. Korea drives on the right side of the road, so the driver's seat is on the left.

examples.en: I eat injeolmi coated generously with soybean powder.
Injeolmi is chewy and nutty, so I eat it often.
My grandmother made injeolmi for me herself.
I bought a pack of injeolmi at the rice cake shop.
Shaved ice made with injeolmi is popular.

examples.ko: 시장에서 인절미가 갓 나와서 하나 샀어요.
examples.en: Fresh injeolmi had just come out at the market, so I bought one.

explain: 찹쌀로 만든 떡에 콩가루를 묻힌 대표적인 한국 떡이에요. 콩가루는 '콩고물'이라고도 해요. 요즘은 '인절미 맛' 라떼나 아이스크림처럼 맛 이름으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I ate injeolmi as a snack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation.

phrases.en: You coat the rice cake in bean powder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인절미를 만드는 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing how injeolmi is made.

phrases.en: I bought injeolmi-flavored ice cream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛 이름으로 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a flavor name.

explain_en: It is a classic Korean rice cake made from glutinous rice and coated in soybean powder. The powder is also called '콩고물'. These days the name is also used as a flavor, as in injeolmi latte or ice cream.

examples.en: My desk has been tidied up neatly.
Once the room is tidy, let's have tea together.
My thoughts got organized, so I took notes.

examples.ko: 짐이 모두 정리될 때까지 며칠 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a few days until all the luggage is sorted.
There are too many unorganized documents.

examples.ko: 문제가 잘 정리되고 나니 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: Now that the issue is sorted out, I feel at ease.

explain: 내가 치우는 건 '정리하다', 저절로 깔끔해진 상태는 '정리되다'예요. 물건뿐 아니라 '생각이 정리되다'처럼 머릿속이 정돈될 때도 써요. 발음은 [정니되다]예요.

phrases.en: My thoughts became clear after talking with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복잡하던 머릿속이 깔끔해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a messy mind becomes clear.

phrases.en: The documents are organized by date.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 깔끔하게 놓여 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the current neat state of things.

phrases.en: My room is messy, so it won't get organized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치우려 해도 깔끔해지지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things stay messy even though you try to tidy up.

explain_en: When you tidy something yourself, it is 정리하다. 정리되다 describes the state of having become neat. It works for objects and also for the mind, as in 생각이 정리되다. It is pronounced [정니되다].

examples.ko: 영화 볼 때 쥐포를 구워 먹었어요.
examples.en: I grilled and ate dried filefish while watching a movie.

examples.ko: 쥐포는 불에 구우면 고소한 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: Dried filefish gives off a savory smell when grilled over a fire.
I bought a bag of dried filefish at the market.

examples.ko: 쥐포가 너무 딱딱해서 잘게 찢어 먹었어요.
examples.en: The dried filefish was too hard, so I tore it into small pieces to eat.

examples.ko: 동생은 쥐포에 마요네즈를 찍어 먹는 걸 좋아해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling likes dipping dried filefish in mayonnaise.
The smell of grilling dried filefish spread all the way down the alley.

explain: 쥐치라는 생선을 납작하게 말려 만든 간식이에요. 보통 불에 살짝 구워서 찢어 먹고, 마요네즈나 고추장에 찍어 먹기도 해요.

phrases.en: When you grill dried filefish over a fire, it smells savory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쥐포는 보통 구워서 먹기 때문에 '굽다'와 가장 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is usually eaten grilled, so it pairs most often with 'to grill'.

phrases.en: I tore the dried filefish by hand and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구운 쥐포를 먹는 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes how people eat grilled dried filefish.

phrases.en: Dipping dried filefish in mayonnaise tastes good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쥐포와 자주 같이 먹는 소스를 말하는 짧은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase for a sauce often eaten with it.

explain_en: It is a snack made by drying filefish (쥐치) into a flat sheet. It is usually lightly grilled and torn into strips, and some people dip it in mayonnaise or red pepper paste.

examples.en: I was so happy when I received the certificate of acceptance.
Please keep your certificate safe.
Yesterday my certificate arrived by mail.

examples.ko: 등록할 때 합격증 사본을 내야 해요.
examples.en: I have to submit a copy of the acceptance certificate when I register.
My name is written on the certificate.

examples.ko: 합격증으로 등록 절차를 밟을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can go through the registration procedure with the certificate.

explain: 시험이나 입학, 자격 심사에 붙었다는 것을 보여 주는 종이나 증명서예요. 합격했다는 소식을 알리는 글은 '합격 통지서'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I received the notice of acceptance yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합격 소식을 알리는 글이에요. 합격증은 합격을 증명하는 종이예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A document announcing a pass. 합격증 is the paper that proves it.

phrases.en: I passed the exam and received a certificate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, with 받다.

phrases.en: Please submit your certificate to the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입학이나 서류 절차에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in admission or paperwork procedures.

explain_en: It is a paper or document proving you passed an exam, admission or qualification review. A notice informing you of the result is also called a '합격 통지서'.

examples.en: I'm happy because I bought a used book cheaply.
Even a used book can be given as a gift if it is clean.
I sell books I've finished reading to a secondhand bookstore.
I like the smell of old books, so I go often.

examples.ko: 이 헌책에는 누가 쓴 메모가 있어요.
examples.en: This used book has notes someone wrote in it.
I studied with a used book instead of a new one.

explain: '헌-'은 낡고 오래된 것 앞에 붙어서 '헌 옷', '헌책'처럼 써요. 반대말은 '새 책'이고, 말할 때는 '중고책'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Used books are cheap, so I like them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헌책'과 거의 같은 뜻이고 사고파는 물건으로 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 헌책; often used when talking about buying and selling.

phrases.en: I sold the old books I had finished reading.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다 읽은 책을 팔 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when selling books you have already read.

phrases.example: 헌책 말고 새 책을 사고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to buy a new book, not a used one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헌책'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 헌책.

explain_en: The prefix '헌-' attaches to worn, old things, as in '헌 옷' and '헌책'. The opposite is '새 책', and people also say '중고책' in speech.
